paragraphs.paragraph: All the people gathered together as one man into the street before the water gate and asked Ezra to bring the book of the law. Ezra read from a wooden pulpit, and the people responded with reverence, blessing, “Amen,” and worship.
paragraphs.title: The Assembly for the Torah Reading

answers: In the street before the water gate
easy.explanation: The people gathered in the street that was before the water gate.
easy.q: Where did all the people gather?

easy.explanation: Ezra the priest brought the law before the congregation.
easy.q: Who brought the book of the law before the congregation?

easy.explanation: When Ezra opened the book, all the people stood up.
easy.q: What did all the people do when Ezra opened the book?

medium.explanation: Ezra stood upon a pulpit of wood made for the purpose.
medium.q: What was the pulpit made of?

answers: They answered, “Amen, Amen,” lifted their hands, and worshipped
medium.explanation: The people answered, “Amen, Amen,” lifted their hands, bowed their heads, and worshipped the LORD.
medium.q: How did the people respond after Ezra blessed the LORD?

answers: Men, women, and all who could hear with understanding
medium.explanation: The law was read before men and women, and all that could hear with understanding.
medium.q: Who heard the reading of the law?

answers: The people gathered, asked for the law, and Ezra read it
Ezra read, the people asked for the law, and then they gathered
The people worshipped, Ezra built the gate, and then he read
challenge.explanation: The people first gathered and asked Ezra to bring the book; afterward, Ezra read it.
challenge.q: Which order correctly describes the beginning of the event?

answers: They responded with reverence and participation
They wanted the reading to stop
challenge.explanation: They stood, answered “Amen,” lifted their hands, bowed, and worshipped.
challenge.q: What does the people’s response show about their attitude toward the reading?

answers: To provide an elevated place for reading the law
challenge.explanation: Ezra stood upon it so that he could read the book before the people.
challenge.q: What was the purpose of the wooden pulpit?

paragraphs.idea: All the people gathered together as one man into the street before the water gate and asked Ezra to bring the book of the law. Ezra read from a wooden pulpit, and the people responded with reverence, blessing, “Amen,” and worship.

paragraphs.paragraph: The Levites caused the people to understand the law by reading distinctly and giving the sense. When the people wept, Nehemiah, Ezra, and the Levites reminded them that the day was holy and directed them to eat, share with the needy, and rejoice.
paragraphs.title: Explaining the Torah and Turning Mourning into Joy

easy.explanation: Jeshua and the Levites caused the people to understand the law.
easy.q: Who caused the people to understand the law?

easy.explanation: All the people wept when they heard the words of the law.
easy.q: How did the people react when they heard the words of the law?

easy.explanation: They were told to eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to those for whom nothing was prepared.
easy.q: What were the people told to do?

answers: Because the day was holy unto the LORD
Because there was no law that day
medium.explanation: Nehemiah, Ezra, and the Levites said, “This day is holy unto the LORD your God.”
medium.q: Why were the people told not to mourn or weep?

medium.explanation: The people were told to eat the fat and drink the sweet.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “the sweet” refer to?

answers: By sending portions to those for whom nothing was prepared
By dividing the book of the law
medium.explanation: They were commanded to send portions to people who had nothing prepared.
medium.q: How were the people to include those in need in their rejoicing?

answers: From weeping and sorrow to rejoicing
challenge.explanation: The people first wept, but afterward went to eat, drink, share, and make great mirth.
challenge.q: What change took place in the people’s emotions?

answers: Understanding caused the people to leave
The people rejoiced because they understood the words declared to them
Understanding caused them to continue weeping
challenge.explanation: They made great mirth because they had understood the words declared unto them.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between understanding and joy?

answers: The joy given by the LORD strengthens the people
The joy of the LORD commanded them to go to war
challenge.explanation: The saying encouraged the people not to grieve but to be strengthened through holy joy.
challenge.q: What does “the joy of the LORD is your strength” mean in context?

paragraphs.idea: The Levites caused the people to understand the law by reading distinctly and giving the sense. When the people wept, Nehemiah, Ezra, and the Levites reminded them that the day was holy and directed them to eat, share with the needy, and rejoice.

paragraphs.paragraph: On the second day, the chief fathers, priests, and Levites gathered to understand the words of the law. They found the command concerning the feast of booths, proclaimed it throughout the cities, and the people gathered branches and built booths on roofs, in courtyards, and in public places.
paragraphs.title: Rediscovering the Festival of Booths and Preparing for It

answers: The chief fathers, priests, and Levites
Only the people near the water gate
easy.explanation: The chief of the fathers, the priests, and the Levites gathered unto Ezra.
easy.q: Who gathered on the second day to understand the law?

answers: To dwell in booths during the feast
easy.explanation: They found that the children of Israel should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month.
easy.q: What command did they find written in the law?

easy.explanation: They brought olive, pine, myrtle, palm, and thick branches.
easy.q: What did the people gather to build the booths?

answers: They studied to understand the words of the law
medium.explanation: They gathered together to understand the words of the law.
medium.q: What did the chief fathers, priests, and Levites do after gathering to Ezra?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to leafy branches used in making the booths.
medium.q: What does “branches of thick trees” describe?

answers: They built booths, found the command, and then heard it
They learned the command, gathered branches, and built booths
They sent portions, built a wall, and then gathered branches
medium.explanation: The command was found and proclaimed; then the people brought branches and made booths.
medium.q: Which sequence correctly describes the people’s actions?

answers: The command was practiced only at the temple
The command belonged only to the priests
The people practiced it in private and public places
challenge.explanation: Booths were made on roofs, in courts, in the courts of the house of God, and in streets.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the places where the booths were built?

answers: It led to proclaiming the command and preparing booths
It canceled the feast of booths
It caused the people to stop studying
challenge.explanation: After finding the command, the leaders proclaimed it and the people prepared booths.
challenge.q: Why was finding the command in the law important?

answers: It was told only to Ezra
It was published and proclaimed in all the cities and in Jerusalem
It was told only to the chief fathers
challenge.explanation: The command was published and proclaimed in all their cities and in Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What shows that the announcement was widespread?

paragraphs.idea: On the second day, the chief fathers, priests, and Levites gathered to understand the words of the law. They found the command concerning the feast of booths, proclaimed it throughout the cities, and the people gathered branches and built booths on roofs, in courtyards, and in public places.

paragraphs.paragraph: All the congregation that had returned from captivity made booths and sat under them, and there was very great gladness. The book of the law was read day by day during the seven-day feast, and on the eighth day there was a solemn assembly according to the manner.
paragraphs.title: The Joy of Sukkot and Continued Torah Reading

answers: All the congregation that returned from captivity
easy.explanation: All the congregation that came again out of the captivity made booths and sat under them.
The passage says, “And there was very great gladness.”
easy.q: How is the people’s joy described?

answers: Day by day throughout the seven-day feast
easy.explanation: It was read each day from the first day unto the last day of the feast.
easy.q: When was the book of the law read?

answers: The first reading of the law
medium.explanation: On the eighth day was a solemn assembly, according unto the manner.
medium.q: What took place on the eighth day?

answers: It happened every year without exception
It had not been done in this way since the days of Jeshua the son of Nun
Only the priests dwelt in booths
medium.explanation: The passage says that since the days of Jeshua the son of Nun, Israel had not done so until that day.
medium.q: What was unusual about dwelling in booths at that time?

answers: The law was read while the people dwelt in booths and rejoiced
medium.explanation: The people dwelt in booths with great gladness, while the law was read throughout the feast.
medium.q: How are the reading of the law and the feast connected?

answers: The feast was only for individuals
The whole community participated in the command
The feast took place only near the water gate
challenge.explanation: All the congregation that returned from captivity made booths and sat under them.
challenge.q: What does the participation of the whole congregation show?

answers: According to what had been prescribed
According to a custom found only in Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The solemn assembly was held according to the prescribed manner.
challenge.q: What does “according unto the manner” mean here?

answers: One day of reading followed by one day of feasting
Seven days of the feast and reading, followed by an assembly on the eighth day
Eight days of feasting without reading the law
challenge.explanation: The law was read during the seven days of the feast, and the eighth day had a solemn assembly.
challenge.q: What time pattern is presented in these verses?

paragraphs.idea: All the congregation that had returned from captivity made booths and sat under them, and there was very great gladness. The book of the law was read day by day during the seven-day feast, and on the eighth day there was a solemn assembly according to the manner.
